articles.title: 10 last-minute fantasy football draft tips, from knowing the rules to not falling in love with your bench
articles.summary: Be sure to consider these last-minute tips heading into your fantasy football draft.
articles.body:
No big introduction needed today. It's the biggest fantasy football draft weekend of the year. Let's get you ready. If you're looking for my key takeaways from drafting each position, head here .

These are standard every year, but they're worth repeating:

The first thing you need to do is thoroughly audit your league settings. I know this isn't always the most fun thing to do — often the league constitutions are dry and a little arduous to sort through. But you gotta know the rules.

Shortly after that, take note of the league calendar and cadences. Take all the free agent deadline settings and put them in your calendar. Everyone has a dynamic and complicated life these days. "Oh, I'll remember that" is no longer a realistic concept. Routine and organization are always your friend.

Make a draft plan, sure, but set it in pencil. You want to be ready to pounce on surprise opportunities at the draft table. I'm always looking to get as much value as I can on that day, with the eye of balancing my roster later.

Constantly be filling your queue during the draft process. You should have key players ready to go if needed, and you also want to be covered if you get bumped offline during the draft. A pad of scrap paper to the side can also be helpful.

I like to play fantasy football with a microscope, not a telescope. Let's focus on what's in front of us. Let's try to win the opening 4-5 week segment. The NFL is such a snow globe league, it's usually a mistake to look too far ahead.

I'm not the type to insure my running backs in August, but I'll likely shift that idea around midseason — when my winning scenarios are more defined and league backup situations are clearer as well. Roster construction takes on a much different shape in the second half of the year.

7. Trade season offers chance to improve

Don't sweat the bye weeks when they arrive in October. Bye week season is trading season, a good opportunity to self-scout your roster and start making some moves that fit your immediate (or long-term) needs. Fantasy trades rarely happen in early September because managers still love their teams. A poker game doesn't really start until a few players get stuck, and the same idea carries over to fantasy football.

I know they will find me soon enough. Injury optimism is rarely your friend in fantasy football. A hurt player might need a "prove-it" week or two before you feel confident starting him. Perhaps they'll be on a limited snap count when they return. The picture often takes too long to develop. New Orleans rookie WR Jordyn Tyson, for one example, is basically off my board. I'm not waiting two-plus months.

The bottom part of your roster is your churn zone, where you should be regularly considering free-agent moves. It's usually a mistake to fall in love with the bottom of your bench. Pickup information we gain in the actual season is usually worth more than speculative and theoretical information that we consider all summer. Remember the lesson of the Monty Hall Problem — once more information becomes available to us, it's usually a good idea to change course, since we're making an information based on additional knowledge.

Just play the Week 1 schedule with defenses, then stream. The Chargers (hosting Arizona) and Jaguars (hosting Cleveland) look good for the opener.

If you had an early draft, it likely made sense to avoid drafting a defense or kicker, with the idea that you'd get one more shot at an impactful field player. But when you draft close to the season, you might as well fill your roster.

articles.title: Las número uno vuelven a ganar a sus 'bestias negras' para campeonar en Madrid
articles.standfirst: Triay y Brea remontaron para ser campeonas del P1 de Madrid y estirar su distancia en la lucha por el número uno.
articles.summary: Triay y Brea remontaron para ser campeonas del P1 de Madrid y estirar su distancia en la lucha por el número uno.
articles.body: Las número uno remontan Hay momentos y torneos que marcan una temporada. Este año, en los más decisivos, ha aparecido un denominador común: la mejor versión de Gemma Triay (34 años, Menorca) y Delfi Brea (26 años, Buenos Aires). En Madrid, la dupla número uno ha vuelto a vencer a sus más inmediatas perseguidoras, con remontada incluida, para ampliar aún más su ventaja en el ranking (desde este lunes la diferencia será de 2.460 puntos en la Race). Con ello, envían un mensaje contundente al resto del circuito: estando físicamente plenas y con un nivel de regularidad altísimo, son prácticamente invencibles. Se impusieron por 6-7 (5), 6-3 y 6-3 ante Bea González y Paula Josemaría, quienes ven cómo la distancia respecto a Triay y Brea es cada vez mayor, justo en la antesala del segundo Major de la temporada (que se disputará la próxima semana en París). Este triunfo supone, además, el sexto título del año para la dupla dirigida por Seba Nerone, que ha fijado un listón de regularidad inalcanzable para el resto: han disputado 13 finales en 15 torneos. Por si fuera poco, han vuelto a derrotar a quienes fueron sus «bestias negras» durante el primer semestre. Hasta julio mantenían un balance negativo frente a ellas, pero los últimos dos enfrentamientos han caído del lado de Triay y Brea: este último y el de Málaga, donde la definición fue aún más ajustada (7-5, 3-6 y 7-6 [3]). El primer set estuvo marcado por los breaks y contrabreaks. No fue hasta el 5-4 cuando González y Josemaría lograron ponerse por delante por primera vez, aunque tuvieron que llegar al tie break para adjudicarse la manga con remontada incluida (estaban 2-5 abajo y endosaron un parcial de 5-0 para cerrarlo por 7-5). Sin embargo, la historia fue muy distinta en el segundo y tercer parcial. Resulta digno de destacar la fortaleza mental de la pareja número uno, que, aun tras el mazazo de perder el primer set, se mantuvo concentrada y logró desplegar su mejor nivel. «Lo más difícil en el pádel es entrar sin buenas sensaciones e ir encontrándolas en el partido, más en una final. En las semifinales salió todo rodado, pero hoy tuvimos que ir creciendo en el durante. Tiene mucho mérito lo que conseguimos», explicó la drive argentina ante los micrófonos de Premier Padel. Por su parte, con la victoria de hoy, Triay se ha convertido en la primera jugadora en alcanzar las 200 victorias en Premier Padel.

articles.title: Position Grades: Marshall
articles.summary: Might we have a Straight-A report card??
articles.body:
Welcome back to another fine season of Position Grades! Per usual, my grades will either be too harsh, too lenient, or just right, depending on your point of view. As always, feel free to drop your takes in the comments section below, but let's get right to dissecting one of the most satisfying head coaching debuts in program history, shall we?

Can you really ask for a better Blue and White debut than that of Rocco Becht's? Throwing for nearly 300 yards and four touchdowns in just 18 passes feels like the very definition of efficiency. Getting Alex Manske into the game by mid-third quarter was especially clutch for his development as he continues his incredible comeback from open heart surgery. And if that wasn't enough, we even got a Connor Barry sighting towards the very end of the game.

Offensive coordinator Taylor Mouser said earlier in the week that he planned to play all four running backs, and he was a man of his word. Carson Hansen lacked "pop" but he sure came up with one of the most clutch runs of the game, taking a 4th-and-1 snap from PSU's own red zone 10 yards to move the chains, in a drive that ultimately finished in the end zone for seven more points. James Peoples showed a little more burst, but the vision could've used some work. Quinton Martin and Cam Wallace both scored TD's, with Martin arguably looking like the most assertive and polished of all four running backs, showing little hesitation in hitting the holes that his offensive line was providing him. Here's to Quinton getting a bit more run going forward…

Koby Howard's 161 yards receiving were the most by a PSU receiver since Parker Washington put up 179 against Ohio State in 2022. Brett Eskildsen also showed off that track speed by taking a screen pass to the end zone for six, Chase Sowell had a pair of catches early on to move the chains, and Zay Robinson made the most of his lone catch by taking it 39 yards to the house. For a room that had been much maligned and missing in action for a good chunk of the last few years, it was refreshing to see the wideouts get open, catch the ball, and rack up some serious YAC.

It may have been a quieter afternoon on the receiving front, but Ben Brahmer had a TD catch late in the first half to give PSU a comfy 24-0 halftime cushion, while Andrew Rappleyea picked up some serious YAC for an 18-yard reception. On the blocking front, both tight ends were pretty solid.

A great day overall for the O-line, allowing just one sack and allowing Rocco Becht to remain in the pocket and scan the field for an open receiver. I know some folks are going to mention the lack of explosiveness in the run game, but I blame that more on Marshall's defense stacking the box and selling out to stop the run and force Becht and the receivers to beat them, which in fairness, was a pretty good strategy against PSU the previous few years.

SPOILER ALERT: The entire defense is getting straight A's, as is the case whenever they pitch a shutout. Caleb Bacon showed that moving him permanently to defensive end was the right move by the coaching staff, racking up six total tackles, with three of them for a loss and one sack, as he was all over the Marshall backfield the entire day and had the Thundering Herd quarterback Carlos Del Rio-Wilson scrambling for his life. Yvan Kemajou also dialed up some nice pressure on the other end, and bigger dudes in the middle at defensive tackle made running the ball a lot more difficult for the guys in green.

Tony Rojas led the team in tackles with seven of them, including two for a loss and a sack, but everyone is talking about Kooper Ebel, who was tremendous in his first game as the "Mike" linebacker and was flying to the ball to either make or assist on a stop.

Marshall's longest completed pass from scrimmage went just 14 yards, and while part of that is due to the front seven generating tons of pressure, it's also due to the secondary covering Marshall's receivers like a fire blanket on a kitchen fire. They did nearly get burned over the top at the end of the half, but thankfully Del Rio-Wilson couldn't quite put the right amount of touch on the ball. Otherwise, a pretty flawless game from the secondary. Shout-out to Bryson Williams, who had an incredible diving interception late in the game.

I've said it ad nauseam on here and on our YouTube show (please subscribe, if you haven't already), but Ryan Barker may have been the most important keep from last offseason, and he showed it by calmly nailing 38-yard field goal on PSU's opening drive, which was aided by a nice 34-yard kickoff return by Zay Robinson. Nathan Tiyce was solid in his debut at punter, with a long of 55 yards and also putting a punt deep inside the Marshall red zone. In addition to his kickoff return, Robinson also had a 23-yard punt return that set PSU up nicely.

For all the wonderful things we read and saw that Matt Campbell and this coaching staff were doing from the time they arrived last December leading up through Fall camp, Nittany Nation was still holding its collective breath when it came to what the actual on-field product would look like in live game action. Well, we got a definitive answer yesterday in the best way imaginable. Seeing Taylor Mouser going downfield in the passing game early and often felt like a breath of fresh air after being subjected to the horror's of Andy Kotelnicki's "horizontal air raid" last season, as was seeing wide receivers who ran crisp routes and got open enough to make plays, not to mention the defense flying around and playing with a real sense of purpose, dictating the game on their terms. I'd also be remiss if I didn't shout out Matt Campbell for celebrating like a teenager who just won the national championship in EA Sports' College Football 27 after a perfect use of a timeout to freeze Marshall's kicker right before halftime.

Yes, it's only one game, and we will find out what this team is truly made of when they face some adversity, but if they showcase the attitude and coaching prowess that was only display yesterday, then you should be feeling a tad more optimistic.

It was pointed out by numerous folks on social media yesterday that the Beaver Stadium sound system at one point during a TV timeout played "Since You've Been Gone", "We're Never Getting Back Together", and "Enter Sandman" consecutively. Whoever is responsible for putting together the music on gameday, a tip of the cap to you, good sir/madam, because that is some A-plus level of trolling!

articles.title: Tymek Kucharczyk wins Laguna Seca finale as Nikita Johnson clinches Indy NXT title
articles.summary: Kucharczyk led all 30 laps from pole for his second victory of the season, while Johnson finished runner-up to secure the championship by 29 points
articles.body:
Tymek Kucharczyk went flag-to-flag from pole to win the second leg of the Indy NXT season finale doubleheader at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca, while Nikita Johnson stayed clear of trouble to capture the championship.

Polish native Kucharczyk, driving the #71 entry for HMD Motorsports, was untouchable throughout all 30 laps, coasting to 6.5765s victory over Johnson on the 11-turn, 2.238-mile natural terrain road course. It marked his second win of the season, solidifying third in the overall standings.

"Yeah, really proud of the work," Kucharczyk said. "Everyone in the team did amazing. The car was really great. Obviously, a big congratulations to Nikita. Big congratulations to Enzo (Fittipaldi) as well. Championship has been very long and very strong. What can I say? What if yesterday didn't happen (being spun from second), but nevertheless, really, really proud. Today, we maximized what we had. I was pushing every lap. I left nothing on the table, so really proud. It was an amazing year."

For Johnson, who started fifth in the #21 Cape Motorsports by ECR entry, the result didn't come without some opening lap drama as he had to dodge a crash right at the green flag. After avoiding the incident, he moved into second and held the position to the finish. The Florida native ended his championship campaign with two wins, nine podiums, along with finishing top 10 in all 18 races.

"It's amazing," said Johnson, 18. "It's good to finally show my emotions. I think a lot of people thought I was passionless, but I'm just emotionless when I drive, right? I just go out there and do the work. And I'm happy that the work's done. Now, I can finally go celebrate."

Lochie Hughes (Andretti Global) took the third and final podium spot.

As Johnson's main title rival coming into the race, Enzo Fittipaldi (HMD Motorsports) mounted a recovery drive from 12th on the grid. The Brazilian-American made aggressive moves in the charge into the top five, but in the end was left finishing fifth. He finished second in the championship, 29 points behind Johnson.

Kucharczyk led the field to the green flag, but an incident immediately followed as Race 1 winner Josh Pierson (Andretti Global) was hit from behind by Max Garcia (Abel Motorsports) and spun from second, collecting Niels Koolen (Chip Ganassi Racing).

The top five after the incident were Kucharczyk, Garcia, Johnson, Hughes, and Jacob Abel (Abel Motorsports). However, Garcia was hit with a stop and hold penalty by Race Control as a result of the contact at the start, elevating Johnson and others up one spot.

Kucharczyk led the field to the restart on Lap 5. Despite starting 12th, Fittipaldi was already up to sixth.

By Lap 10, Johnson was under threat by Hughes for the runner-up spot, while Kucharczyk's lead widened to 3.5192s. Fittipaldi climbed up to fifth.

Kucharczyk's lead over Johsnon was 5.0201s at the halfway point. Hughes, Abel, and Fittipaldi continued to run third through fifth.

With 10 laps to go, the frontrunners were more strung out as Kucharczyk's lead reached 6.5480s over Johnson.

Fittipaldi began to hound the rear wing of Abel with nine laps to go, and attempted an unsuccessful move at the Zanardi Corkscrew.

Kucharczyk continued to extend his advantage, holding a 7.6539s lead over Johnson with five laps to go.

Kucharczyk remained clear to the chequered flag, winning by 6.5765s as Johnson's second place secured the 2026 Indy NXT championship.

articles.title: Why Dodgers' Shohei Ohtani has likely already lost NL MVP to Pete Crow-Armstrong
articles.summary: The Dodgers' two-way superstar is not likely to win the NL MVP this season.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers might be the World Series favorites still, but there is some real concern about Shohei Ohtani , who's been out for a few games in a row and has a setback in his attempt to return to the mound.

It's a big loss for the Dodgers to not have Ohtani pitching for them after initially having Cy Young-caliber numbers through July. But it's also now become an issue at the plate, as he's not been in the lineup for a few days now.

Unfortunately for the Dodgers and Ohtani, as USA Today's Bob Nightengale notes, this recent setback and absence from the lineup have likely ended the National League MVP debate, with Pete Crow-Armstrong practically guaranteed to win the award now.

Shohei Ohtani likely already lost NL MVP to Pete Crow-Armstrong

"It was an unbelievable run, but Shohei Ohtani's bid for a fourth consecutive MVP award is over, with his recent struggles with nagging injuries preventing him from returning to the mound," Nightengale writes. "It's Pete Crow-Armstrong's award to lose."

Ohtani has posted 6.5 bWAR this season and has been one of the best players in baseball overall. Even though he's missed some time and hasn't pitched since early July, his season-long numbers are more than good enough to justify MVP votes.

The only issue for Ohtani is that Crow-Armstrong has been on an all-time heater this season. He has put up 8.6 bWAR for the Chicago Cubs so far, and has plenty of incredible statistics to warrant an MVP bid; it's his for the taking.

For Ohtani to win this award, PCA would have to go into a major slump to end the season, and Ohtani would need to return and have one of the best months of his MLB career at the plate.

A return to the mound is unlikely, which has already effectively cemented his status as the runner-up to Crow-Armstrong in the MVP race. Combined now with his absence from the lineup, Ohtani's odds have, understandably, plummeted.

He was the far-and-away best player in the first half of the 2026 MLB season, but with under a month to go, Ohtani has fallen to second fiddle behind Crow-Armstrong.

Crow-Armstrong's offensive bWAR this season is 7.1, while his defensive bWAR is 1.9. Ohtani only has 3.6 offensive bWAR and -1.2 defensive bWAR as a full-time DH. His 3.0 pitching bWAR won't be enough to make up the difference.

It's unfortunate, but barring a miracle, it's looking like Ohtani will miss out on the NL MVP this season, with Crow-Armstrong's production being too great for Ohtani to match as the 2026 MLB season comes to a close.

articles.title: UCLA Starts Bob Chesney Era With Big Win Over Cal
articles.summary: UCLA kicked off the Bob Chesney Era with a big win against a rival in Cal, going on the road to start this new chapter of Bruin footbal. The post UCLA Starts...
articles.body:
UCLA kicked off the Bob Chesney Era with a big win against a rival in Cal, going on the road to start this new chapter of Bruin football.

UCLA was the underdog entering the game, though it was relatively even before kickoff. Cal boasts Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele, one of the best quarterbacks in college football, along with former Oregon defensive coordinator Tosh Lupoi as the head coach.

Cal had all the motivation to start a new era with a win, but UCLA created havoc defensively, forcing three turnovers while also running a competent offense.

Nico Iamaleava went 14 for 22 with 184 passing yards and an interception, not his best game, but the Bruins built their offense through the run.

UCLA rushed for 277 yards, using three different running backs and asking Iamaleava to step up as well to run when needed.

It was Wayne Knight and Anthony Woods who had five touchdowns among themselves, and they rushed for 189 yards just between the pair of them.

Along with two interceptions from secondary member Ta'Shawn James, UCLA was able to capitalize on Cal's mistakes.

"The word is the resolve of the team, and you felt it shift a little bit on the sideline at one point and got it a tie game, so it's not like we were in a tough spot; we just needed to make sure we maximized our next opportunity and these guys never wavered," Chesney said after the game.

Iamaleava suffered a leg injury on a running play, which left him limping and eventually unable to move on the ground, though the signal caller reports he is okay after getting beat up on the bottom of a pile.

"His calf kind of got cleated, so he tried – it just kept cramping up … so we've got to do some work on that and get that cleaned up," Chesney said of Nico Iamaleava.

Overall, it wasn't the kind of start Iamaleava would have wanted, but it was good enough to win a game and give him something to work on going forward.

articles.title: 'It's our song;' Oregon not amused by Boise State celebration during 'Shout!'
articles.summary: With the game tied entering the fourth quarter, Boise State danced to "Shout!" and added some motivation for the Oregon Ducks to win the game.
articles.body:
Not many expected a tie game at the end of the third quarter at Autzen Stadium. The Oregon Ducks entered the season opener against Boise State as heavy favorites and could have used the quarter to experiment with different players in a potential blowout.

And, as they usually do, the Ducks could have danced and celebrated to "Shout!" which is always played at the end of the third quarter.

Instead, the Ducks found themselves in a dogfight with an unranked foe, and it was the Broncos who were dancing.

The Ducks slumbered along the sideline, walking to the other end of the field, while Boise State's sideline turned into the Delta House from the film 'Animal House', parading the field and leaping with joy as the possible upset loomed.

That didn't sit well with the Ducks just across the field, many of whom saw the celebration and used it as fuel for the final 15 minutes. Oregon quarterback Dante Moore followed the event with a pair of scoring drives, including a 62-yard strike to Dakorien Moore for the eventual winning score.

"It was funny that they did the 'Shout!'" Moore said. "It was a little weird, but hey, who knows. It was like, 'Hey, you can't do that in our home. So we made sure that we go out there and capitalize and finish drives and put some points on the board."

Just two years ago, when Moore was sitting as the backup behind Dillon Gabriel , Oregon had a similar strategy on the road at Wisconsin. Instead of letting the "Jump Around" moment at the end of the third quarter pump up the crowd and deflate their sideline, the Ducks danced and embraced it.

Moore recognized the contradiction, but understood the drive behind it as a visiting team walking into hostile territory.

"They were just doing something that we've done before, and that's just trying to flip your mind when you're playing away to try to steal the juice from the crowd," Moore said. "We seen it. We laughed at it. We went out there and put points on the board."

Boise State head coach Spencer Danielson said it was something the Broncos had been planning for weeks to find a way to finish strong. Unfortunately for the upset-minded Broncos, the plan seemed to backfire.

The Broncos had a long drive for a field goal to start the final quarter, but went three-and-out and succumbed to Oregon's pass rush on the final drive before turning the ball over on downs to effectively end the game.

Moore said the moment motivated Oregon's sideline to finish the game strong and own the field. The Oregon quarterback finished the game with a career-high 378 passing yards and three touchdowns.

It especially motivated tight end Jamari Johnson , who was none too pleased by the Broncos' antics, according to Moore's recollection.

"(Johnson) was screaming at me, like, 'This is some BS,'" Moore recalled.

"They were having their fun, but I kind of took it as a little disrespect," Johnson said. "It's our song. Y'all don't got no business dancing to our song. They're a great team though, and I give them their props. They play hard. But that was a little funny to see them out there dancing."

The Ducks will celebrate the come-from-behind victory, but there likely won't be much dancing after a sloppy showing to begin the season. Oregon will get a chance to regroup and respond with a better outing in the team's first road test next Saturday at Oklahoma State.

articles.title: Goalkeeper Koeman Jr scores twice in Eredivisie draw
articles.summary: Goalkeeper Ronald Koeman Jr, son of Netherlands legend Ronald Koeman, scores twice for Telstar to rescue a point against Cambuur.
articles.body:
Goalkeeper Ronald Koeman Jr, son of former Netherlands defender Ronald Koeman, scored two goals for Dutch side Telstar to rescue a point in their league match against Cambuur.

Koeman Jr scored two penalties in the 2-2 Eredivisie draw with the second spot-kick coming in the 11th minute of injury time.

The 31-year-old had scored a penalty before, converting the winner in May against FC Volendam to confirm Telstar's safety from relegation.

Telstar had a man sent off in the 22nd minute and conceded two second-half goals to trail visitors Cambuur with less than half an hour to play.

Koeman converted his first penalty on 63 minutes, before his dramatic equaliser in the 101st minute.

He is the first goalkeeper to score twice in an Eredivisie game.

Koeman's father resigned as Netherlands manager in June after their last-32 exit to Morocco at the World Cup.

articles.title: How Rutgers AD Keli Zinn handles Greg Schiano’s future will define her legacy | Politi
articles.summary: Rutgers athletic director Keli Zinn may soon face the difficult process of replacing a longtime football coach — perhaps even during the season.
articles.body:
Days after the unthinkable loss to UMass, the hits were still coming for Rutgers. The hosts of multiple ESPN shows lined up to take their shots , predictable but painful. The trolls and content creators used the aftermath — and, specifically, history's most ill-timed fireworks show — to fill their social media feeds with meme after meme.

Even the head coach of the defending national champions couldn't resist delivering an uppercut. "We all saw Rutgers-UMass, right?" Curt Cignetti asked on national TV before Indiana crushed North Texas on Saturday afternoon, using the Scarlet Knights' 37-21 loss as a cautionary tale for what happens when a Big Ten program doesn't take its nonconference opponents seriously.

That was bad. This is arguably worse: Diehard fans — i.e., the paying customers — are turning their scarlet "R" magnets upside down on the back on their cars and posting photos for the world to see. It would be impossible to overstate just how bad of a loss this was for Greg Schiano.

The vultures will find fresh carrion somewhere else eventually. That doesn't erase the damage that this loss has done to the ongoing efforts — and the real progress — behind the scenes to build Rutgers into college program its alumni can support with pride.

For Keli Zinn, the leader of those endeavors, the job just got much harder. The athletic director entered her second year hoping Schiano would be her chief ally in this Rutgers reclamation project, and instead, the head coach looks like he might be her biggest obstacle.

How Zinn handles the next few months — and what likely will be her biggest single decision — will define her success and her legacy.

No one should feel sorry for Zinn. She signed up for this with her eyes wide open. Even still, it's hard to imagine she had "two-touchdown loss to 0-12 UMass" on her September bingo card. Just hours before that outcome turned Rutgers into a laughingstock again, Zinn set out her clear expectations for the seventh year of Schiano 2.0.

"That is, in its simplest form, is to improve what we saw from last year," she said.

With 11 games left, that's still possible. Schiano was defiant on Thursday night, insisting that one game will not define this team despite the many red flags that were on display for three and a half hours against an opponent paid $1.5 million for the game.

"I've been down this road before," Schiano said. "We know our way out, and we'll get this thing right."

But if Rutgers follows this disastrous loss to UMass with another stink bomb at Boston College on Friday, the writing will be on the wall in bright scarlet paint. Zinn isn't likely make a move on Schiano in Week 2, but with powerhouses USC and Indiana coming to Piscataway over the three weeks that follow, a change will be inevitable.

And, if that happens, Zinn will be on the clock, too. She must first find the resources to pay Schiano's $18 million buyout — a challenge that might be easier than it would seem given a bloated football budget with fat to trim. Rutgers has more than doubled what it spent on football in Schiano's first season to $76 million , a number that's bigger than even what Tennessee and Texas spend.

Even once Zinn figures out the math, she has to find a diplomatic way to make the change with a man who holds an important place in Rutgers history. His 18 seasons, including that one shining moment in '06 against Louisville, has earned Schiano more than an unceremonious pink slip slid under his office door. The emotion that accompanied his return in 2019 doesn't vanish simply because he didn't finish the job.

Can Zinn work out an agreement in which Schiano is fired but coaches the remainder of the season? Would the prideful head coach even entertain that possibility given his history here? These unthinkable questions are on the table now if Rutgers crashes and burns — and they're just the beginning of the challenge facing this AD.

Anyone who followed the last coaching search understands just how difficult it was to get top candidates to even consider this job. Zinn will not only need to find a coach undaunted by the challenge but one who can bring some players — like what Matt Campbell did at Penn State and Bob Chesney accomplished for UCLA last winter — to fill this roster.

She knows she needs the football program to thrive for her to achieve any of her biggest goals in Piscataway. Before the UMassacre ( trademark pending ), Zinn was trumpeting the news that Rutgers had mostly solved the Name, Image and Likeness funding problems that had sent its coaches trudging into competition with both hands tied behind their backs for the past five years.

"I came in at a time when a lot of people talked about Rutgers having an NIL problem," Zinn said on ESPN New York . "We do not have an NIL problem going into Year 2. We now have infrastructure to support exactly what needs to happen there in order for us to be successful in that space."

That's a major development, and one of many. In her first year, Zinn has restructured the athletic department, goosed corporate support and launched plans for much-needed facility upgrades. None of these incremental improvements will matter if the football program is cratering on national TV each weekend, and Zinn knows it.

Even the most loyal Schiano supporters are waiting and wondering what Zinn will do next. If the football team doesn't recover immediately, the athletic director will need to make the kind of legacy-defining leadership change for the team that changes the narrative in Piscataway.

Then — and only then — will the loss to UMass be remembered for something more than just memes and migraines.

articles.title: The stats behind Arsenal’s dominance of Chelsea
articles.summary: Arsenal beat Chelsea 2-1 at the Emirates, but the underlying numbers show a far more dominant display than the scoreline suggests.Photo by Justin Setterfield...
articles.body:
Arsenal beat Chelsea 2-1 at the Emirates, but the underlying numbers show a far more dominant display than the scoreline suggests.

Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images

Arsenal produced a far more dominant performance against Chelsea than the 2-1 scoreline suggested, overturning an early deficit at the Emirates Stadium while controlling the areas of the game that mattered most.

The visitors went ahead after only two minutes when Morgan Rogers found the net from range after Jorrel Hato had won the ball as Arsenal defended poorly, but the Gunners recovered steadily rather than allowing the early goal to alter the shape of the match.

Kai Havertz equalised in the 25th minute against his former club before Martin Odegaard completed the turnaround five minutes into the second half.

His winning goal came from a fast break and was recorded at 0.59 xG and 0.14 xGOT.

Before that, Arsenal had a goal ruled out for offside.

For supporters, the narrow margin made the closing stages feel tighter than the game itself had been. The underlying numbers show Arsenal were comfortably superior in decisive areas.

Arsenal finished with 55 per cent possession and completed 385 of 457 passes at 84 per cent accuracy.

Chelsea completed 309 of 379 at 82 per cent.

The difference was even clearer in the opposition half, where Arsenal completed 265 passes compared with Chelsea's 191.

The quality of the chances was more striking still.

Arsenal produced 2.11 expected goals to Chelsea's 0.35 and created all four of the match's big chances.

Arsenal also registered 45 touches in the Chelsea penalty area, while Chelsea managed just 25 in Arsenal's.

13 of Arsenal's 16 shots came from inside the box, compared with five for Chelsea.

Arsenal had nine efforts on target and forced eight saves from the visiting goalkeeper, while David Raya made four, albeit one of them was world class from Estevao , on as a late second half sub.

The xG breakdown underlined the same pattern.

Arsenal generated 1.45 xG from open play and another 0.66 from set pieces.

Chelsea produced 0.28 from open play and 0.07 from set pieces.

Arsenal's xG on target stood at 2.39, compared with 0.36 for Chelsea.

The visitors did compete well in direct contests. Chelsea edged the overall duel count 43-42 and won 16 aerial duels to Arsenal's 13.

Arsenal, though, were stronger on the ground, winning 29 duels to Chelsea's 27.

Those numbers mattered less than what each side did with possession.

Chelsea's defensive workload reflected Arsenal's sustained pressure. They made six blocks to Arsenal's two and committed 16 fouls, collecting four yellow cards.

Arsenal committed 13 fouls and were booked twice, one of which went to Christos Tzolis for waving an imaginary card.

Chelsea can also consider themselves incredibly fortunate that Cole Palmer , who was booked for a clear pull back to stop a break was not booked minutes earlier for deliberately studding Myles Lewis-Skelly 's Achilles.

Arsenal also covered more ground, 120.2km to Chelsea's 114.1km, while the visitors made 107 sprints to Arsenal's 104, but covered less ground with them (2.7km v 2.6).

The scoreline says Arsenal won by a single goal. The statistics tell a clearer story.

Chelsea scored almost immediately, but Arsenal created every big chance, generated more than six times their xG, spent far more time in dangerous areas and repeatedly forced the visitors back towards their own goal.

It felt close because Arsenal did not make their superiority count more emphatically.

In terms of control and chance creation, it was anything but.

articles.title: Conor McGregor hails Katie Taylor with social media spree
articles.summary: Conor McGregor has praised the work of Katie Taylor with several posts on social media.
articles.body:
Conor McGregor 's unwavering admiration for Katie Taylor was on full display on social media.

On Saturday, September 5, Taylor rolled back the years and brought the curtain down on a legendary career. A fairytale ending is what all fighters wish for, and Taylor was given that in abundance. The Irishwoman handed France's own Flora Pili her first professional loss in a sold-out Croke Park, in her home country. Alongside that, the 40-year-old delivered a near-flawless display in front of a historic crowd of 83,000, breaking the attendance record for an individual female sporting event.

Amid their success in combat sports, Katie Taylor and Conor McGregor have a long history of support for one another. Continuing that tradition, McGregor hailed Taylor after she retired from boxing—even asking her to reconsider her retirement.

"Katie Taylor, let's do ONE MORE FOR THE MAC," McGregor said on X. "Well done, champ, Katie Taylor!"

The praise didn't end there. Conor McGregor posted a direct callback to a compliment Katie Taylor had given him years prior, likening him to the Muhammad Ali of the UFC .

Returning the favor, McGregor grouped the three of them in a post on X as boxing and mixed martial arts icons.

'The Notorious' famously went to support Katie Taylor during her WBA and IBF lightweight world titles defense against Cindy Serrano at the TD Garden in Boston.

Remembering that time, alongside the caption, " Real Love, " McGregor called back to his support of Taylor in 2018.

Continuing in his Muhammad Ali and Katie Taylor admiration, McGregor shared a picture of the two, 54-years apart, in the very same arena.

The post reminisced about Ali's 11th-round knockout of Alvin Lewis and showed an eerily similar picture side by side with Taylor's win on Saturday; both throwing right hands with grimaces on their faces.

articles.title: Yankees Social Media Spotlight: The Wild Wild West
articles.summary: The Yankees spent this past week on the West Coast.
articles.body:
It's Sunday once more, and you know what that means — it's time for our weekly social media roundup! The Yankees have spent the last seven days in the West Coast, hanging in Anaheim as Arte Moreno sold the Los Angeles Angels, then heading on down to San Diego after an offday to take on a bunch of old friends, the Padres. With so much in store, we've got a lot to cover, so let's get started!

Last Sunday afternoon, the Yankees gave the Red Sox a 16-1 bearsown, winning the season rubber match to give them the tiebreaker in case both squads finish the season with identical records (as we saw last year, when the Yankees lost the tiebreaker to Toronto, that can be significant come playoff time). Key to that win was Heliot Ramos, whose big three-run home run marked his first significant Yankees moment. Not surprisingly, he took to Instagram to celebrate after the game.

Late in the game, Boston announcer Will Flemming earned the ire of Yankees fans everywhere, criticizing Jazz Chisholm Jr. with language that has historically been used to criticize Hispanic and Black players, then wishing that the Red Sox drilled Austin Wells and started a fight with Chisholm. Naturally Yankees players and fans took to social media to criticize him — including on his own ""apology."

We had a quite a few game belts this week, with Will Warren, Spencer Jones, and Austin Wells each taking home the honor.

Suzyn Waldman took advantage of the Thursday's offday to hang out in the warm confines of Southern California.

For this week's QOTD, we get to see just how good (or bad) the Yankees are at writing in cursive — I can confirm that it's more rarely taught to students these days, so if you think these may be hard to read at times … yeah, I'm not surprised.

We wrap up this week's roundup with some other photos from around the team.

articles.body:
Juventus take on AC Milan in a clash that promises to be one of the most exciting fixtures in Serie A this season, and this is the team announced by Luciano Spalletti.

Juve and Milan have made identical starts to the campaign, with both teams looking to maintain their winning runs. The Bianconeri will be keen to win their first head-to-head clash of the term and establish themselves as the stronger side.

The Old Lady knows that will be easier said than done, however, and they will need to produce their best performance if they are to secure the result they want. Milan have also started strongly and will arrive at the Allianz Stadium with confidence.

Under Ruben Amorim, Milan have found a formula and shape that can help them perform well and meet expectations. The players have responded positively to his demands so far, giving the manager plenty of reason to believe they can continue their strong start.

Juve know they will not find it easy against a Milan side that has started the campaign well. The Bianconeri will still take confidence from their recent record against their opponents, having avoided defeat in their last six Serie A meetings with Milan.

That record gives Juventus reason to believe they can get another positive result, although past meetings will not decide what happens this weekend. The Old Lady will need to match Milan's intensity and take advantage of their opportunities.

The two clubs could not be separated in either meeting last season, with both matches ending level. That could make this weekend's encounter even more intriguing as both sides look to claim the points.

There is a feeling that this time there could be a winner when Juventus and Milan meet. Neither team will want to surrender their strong start to the campaign, and the importance of the fixture should ensure an intense contest.

For Juventus, victory would reinforce their early progress and give the Bianconeri an important result against one of their expected rivals. Milan will have the same ambition and will want to continue responding to Amorim's demands.

One thing is almost certain before kick-off: this should be a thrilling match between two sides determined to win. The Old Lady will now hope their strong record against Milan continues when the teams meet at the Allianz Stadium.

articles.title: Fernando Alonso Explains His Italian GP DNF as Aston Martin F1 Suffers Another Disaster
articles.summary: Fernando Alonso’s 2026 Italian Grand Prix ended with damage from the second Lesmo, not a mechanical failure from his power unit as viewers expected. The Asto...
articles.body:
Fernando Alonso's 2026 Italian Grand Prix ended with damage from the second Lesmo, not a mechanical failure from his power unit as viewers expected. The Aston Martin driver said a Turn 7 kerb strike changed the car's behavior, leaving him too slow to justify continuing at Monza on the Sunday.

"I think I went off in Turn 7 exit, second over the curb, and since that moment, yeah, the car was not feeling the same anymore, so probably I got some damage underneath and it was not worth keeping on going, you know, we were slow and with damage on the car, no point," Alonso said following the race.

Alonso reported that the issue arose as he exited the second Lesmo corner. He confirmed that the car sustained damage after hitting the curb, which ultimately led to his retirement. He drove Aston Martin's No. 14 car into the garage rather than continue with a car that no longer felt right.

The DNF came after an already complicated weekend . Alonso began the race from the pit lane due to changes made to the power unit by Aston Martin during parc ferme.

That earlier problem was battery-related, according to Alonso.

"Yeah, it was the battery at the end, battery problem . So we changed all the electrical components of the car and today it was fine."

Prior to the race, Aston Martin made some minor suspension adjustments, too.

"Yeah, I think we changed something in the suspension, but minor minor tweaks, nothing really dramatic or experimental, you know, it was a normal setup," he confirmed.

He added that three or six components had been replaced while discussing the battery problem:

"I think we three or six components we changed now, so I think we understand that there is some kind of issue there that we need to fix, not totally solved, but yeah, nothing unexpected."

Alonso Found One Bright Spot Before Looking to Singapore

A red-flag gave Alonso a chance to recover some entertainment from an otherwise miserable afternoon. He said he passed Lance Stroll and Valtteri Bottas, then spent time fighting the Cadillac cars. Sergio Perez was the other Cadillac driver involved in that battle, while Stroll ultimately retired with a hydraulic problem of his own.

"Yeah, it was good. I think we had some fun with the with the Cadillacs, you know, that was kind of unexpected."

"At least we could fight a little bit the Cadillacs and that was maybe unexpected because we thought that we were on our own."

The next race will take place in a week at Spain's new Madring circuit in Madrid.

"Yeah, looking forward, I think from the remaining races, we know that there are weekends that we will be struggling, weekends that will be better. You know, maybe next one is one of the opportunities, so looking forward."

articles.title: Kayvon Thibodeaux Trade: Giants, Patriots Connected In Latest Rumor
articles.summary: Kayvon Thibodeaux could use a change of scenery, as the pass-rushing specialist is buried on the New York Giants depth chart as he enters the final year of h...
articles.body:
Kayvon Thibodeaux could use a change of scenery, as the pass-rushing specialist is buried on the New York Giants depth chart as he enters the final year of his rookie contract. A former top-five pick in the 2022 NFL Draft , the Oregon product started off his career in promising fashion, recording 11.5 sacks during his second year in the league. However, injuries limited the pass rusher to just 22 games over the past two seasons, and he doesn't have the proper environment for a bounce-back season.

Now set to hit free agency after the season, it's hard to envision any way for Kayvon Thibodeaux to see the field on a regular basis. Brian Burns and former third-overall pick Abdul Carter are ahead of him in the pecking order, and first-round pick Arvell Reese will fight for additional snaps. With this in mind, it's easy to see why Kayvon Thibodeaux is a popular trade target. The New York Giants reportedly wanted a second-round pick for his services, and Bleacher Report's Kristopher Knox doesn't think the team will lower its offer any time soon.

"One of the Patriots biggest weaknesses is their pass rush," Knox writes. "While New England did sign Dre'Mont Jones and use a second-round pick on Illinois' Gabe Jacas , it also recorded just 34 sacks as a team last season. If the Patriots' pass rush struggles again early in 2026, don't be shoif they go chasing sack artists on the trade market – and given their desire to avoid the dreaded Super Bowl hangover, don't be surprised if they get a little desperate."

Giants, Patriots Linked In Kayvon Thibodeaux Trade Rumors

It's hard to argue against the reasoning behind a Kayvon Thibodeaux trade. The pass rusher has been an obvious trade target ever since the Giants selected Arvell Reese, but teams like New England could get desperate as the season progresses. Alternatively, the Giants could lower their asking price if they're not in the playoff picture at the trade deadline.

The New York Giants have a new head coach in John Harbaugh and a promising young quarterback in USC's Jaxson Dart . While this team probably won't win the Super Bowl, they have legitimate playoff aspirations, especially if star wide receiver Malik Nabers can stay healthy. Trading Kayvon Thibodeaux doesn't make this team better, and keeping him around for an additional season is more valuable than the late-round pick they'd probably receive for his services. If they're fighting for a Wild Card spot in October, they'll probably keep him. However, if they're staring down another top-10 pick, this trade could happen.

The New England Patriots made the Super Bowl last year, so it's safe to say that they're ahead of schedule in their rebuild. The team still has a budding superstar in Drake Maye under center and the Patriots spent the offseason bolstering his supporting cast. By all accounts, this offense should be one of the best in the league, but they'll need the defense to hold up their end of the bargain. Quite frankly, a Kayvon Thibodeaux trade could go a long way in addressing the biggest flaw on the roster.

New England has a strong secondary (assuming Christian Gonzalez plays), but the pass rush leaves a lot to be desired. Veteran Harold Landry is on the Physically Unable to Perform list, rookie Gabe Jacas did not look good in the preseason, and it's anyone's guess as to how this team will create pressure on the edge. Kayvon Thibodeaux should start for this team and would give New England an adequate pass rush that should be good enough to support this otherwise strong roster.

articles.title: Penn State alum pumps breaks on hype train after Week 1 shutout
articles.summary: Penn State shutout Marshall in its season opener, but former Nittany Lions linebacker Jason Cabinda wants to see them against better teams.
articles.body:
The James Franklin era at Penn State was one that was needed during one of the most tumultuous periods in school history. He stabilized the program, but the two sides just reached a point where they were better off apart after a memorable 11-year partnership.

Franklin's impact is already being felt at Virginia Tech as the team made a statement with a 73-3 blowout win in Week 1. Penn State coach Matt Campbell was no slouch in the season opener either, orchestrating a 45-0 win against Marshall on Saturday.

Unsurprisingly, the two coaches were compared over the weekend, with a notable college football account saying, "This ain't James Franklin's Penn State." Former Nittany Lions linebacker Jason Cabinda responded to the post saying that he was happy the team won, but "they played Marshall."

Cabinda explained in the comments that it wasn't a slight to his old school, but his judgment could be clouded by the fact that he played for Franklin. He would like to see Penn State go against better competition before making a determination of how good they are.

There's no arguing with the idea that a game against Marshall isn't the measuring stick for how this team compares to contenders around the country. However, Saturday's game was a noticeable improvement from how the Nittany Lions played in recent years.

There were countless times when they came out flat and uninspiring against an opponent they should crush. This led to wins that looked comfortable on the scoreboard but were more of a struggle than the naked eye could see.

The new-look Penn State team came out looking to send a message, and they did exactly that. Campbell seems like a no-nonsense guy who is focused on nothing but winning games and looking fundamentally sound doing it. Nobody knows how his tenure with the Nittany Lions will end up compared to Franklin's, but it's off to a better start than most anticipated.

articles.title: Will Stein finds plenty to fix after Kentucky victory
articles.summary: Kentucky football coach Will Stein spoke to the media after their week one win, and had plenty to say.
articles.body:
Ask Kentucky football coach Will Stein how he plans to spend the first night of his head-coaching career, and he starts down one road before swerving onto another: " I'm going to go have a cold beer and f*****g"—he catches himself—"excuse my French, I was going to say F-ing hang out with my family, sorry. Apologize, sorry, Big Blue Nation. They probably liked that."

They probably did. It was the loosest sixty seconds of an otherwise exacting hour, and it tells you almost everything about the version of Stein who just beat Youngstown State 45-13 : a coach with a beer in one hand and a red pen already in the other.

The final score wasn't close. Kentucky ran for 205 yards, threw for 301, and held a legitimately dangerous dual-threat quarterback to 59 yards on 28 carries. Stein gave the opponent his full respect without giving an inch of credit to his own defense's margin for error: "I think that guy can play a lot of different places. Not just in this league, but all over the country. He can run it, he can throw it, and for the most part we stopped him running the ball, which was a big part of the plan. " Praise for the other guy, a checked box for his own game plan, in the same breath—a trick most coaches can't manage after a 32-point win.

What Stein couldn't do, even for one afternoon, was leave well enough alone. Somewhere in the first half of an already comfortable game, his offense huddled a beat too slow. Most coaches forget that by the postgame buffet. Stein brought it up unprompted: "That's where it pisses me off as a coach," he said. "You have to play at a certain standard every single snap. Regardless of circumstances. I don't care if it's hot, and I don't care if it's freezing cold or raining. Sleeting, snowing, you need to get your butt back to the huddle and get to the line of scrimmage ASAP so we can dictate the pace."

Dictating the pace, it turns out, is the whole point of the operation. "We dictate the pace of the game," Stein said. "That's how our offensive is really built. You will see us huddle, you will see us speed break, and you will see us no-huddle. To me, if you just go one pace the whole game, that's where the defense can kind of catch on and get your rhythm. We like to mix it up on people." It's a tempo built to be annoying on purpose—a fitting description, honestly, of Stein's whole news conference for anyone hoping to just enjoy a season-opening blowout in peace.

His new quarterback got the identical treatment his opponent's did: real praise, filed immediately next to real notes. Eighteen-for-27, 304 yards, and four touchdowns in his first career start, and Stein's headline take on it doubled as a syllabus. "That's not how you play quarterback; how you play quarterback is you take the easy money. You take what they give you," he said, before circling back to the compliment. "I thought the majority of the game he managed extremely well. He had a lot of checks and kills built-in. He was able to elude some rushers on nakeds. I think for his first start I was very pleased with his performance."

The running back rotation, at least, went exactly to plan—Stein's plan, specifically . "We really went in this game saying, 'Let's try to get him 12 to 15 carries max,'" he said. "He had nine, which I thought was perfect. " Two true freshmen receivers earned the kind of unscripted enthusiasm that's harder to fake than a compliment on cue. Kenny Darby got it first: " That guy can play football. You can just see it. He's got twitch; he loves the game. He never wants to come out. He's a real deal." Prince Jean got the same file stamped on him minutes later— "He's a real deal," "smart, tough, dependable." A few questions after that, someone brought up freshman linebacker Isaiah McMillan, fresh off five solo tackles, a tackle for loss, and a pass breakup. Stein's answer sounded less like a scouting report than a coach who'd already seen the trailer. "When he got his opportunity in practice, he played the exact same way," he said. "Our second scrimmage, I think he had an interception, he had two fumble recoveries, and he had like seven tackles. I'm like, Dang, let's play this game. He can go." Then, almost on autopilot, the same three words came back out: "He's smart, he's tough, dependable, and really proud of him just stepping up when his number is called."

Even the day's one real offensive hiccup—stretches where the ball didn't find Kentucky's playmakers—got turned into a teaching point instead of a gripe. "I want to credit DJ on that play, too, for the perimeter blocking," Stein said. "When the ball is not coming to you in a game, it can be frustrating. I thought the guys handled adversity in terms of identifying him." Then, on how a receiver is supposed to respond when the ball simply doesn't find him: "You play your ass off, and you go out there, and you block. "No sympathy. Just a standard.

Then, for a few minutes, none of it was about football at all. Stein's father served as Kentucky's honorary captain— "the time we spent here at UK together and being a Letterman," Stein said, "and being the reason why I'm here" —and his wife and kids were waiting on the field afterward. He didn't linger there long before the job pulled him back. "But my kids know their dad, and my wife knows that her husband has got a job to do, " he said, before adding, almost as a correction to himself , "I am really thankful that they are here to support. They are my biggest fans. My wife is my biggest cheerleader. My kids love me no matter what, which is great."

The day's most sober moment had nothing to do with wins or standards. Kentucky honored the memory of Nic Smith with an open locker, an empty seat, and a helmet sticker, and Stein didn't treat it as a ceremony. "I saw his dad before the game walking into the stadium, which was just a reminder about how precious life is," he said. "You know, I've got a little boy, I've got a little girl, and I can't imagine losing them. So we are always going to remember him."

By the time Stein got back around to that beer—the one he'd promised himself and then apologized for wanting—he'd already told the room exactly how long it would last. "I've got to watch it," he said. "But I'm going to grade the ball security, then the effort running to the ball on defense, and the effort chasing the ball on offense harder than anything. And so, that has to improve, I know that. To me, that was where the standard lacked today, and it wasn't for a lack of want to. It's literally we just got to practice running to the ball and chasing the ball on offense better."

Forty-five points on the board, and Kentucky's coach walked out of his own celebration already hunting for what was wrong with it. That, more than the score, is the actual scouting report on Year One. Now the real test starts with Bama next up!

articles.title: Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea: Odegaard winner and Raya heroics settle thrilling London derby
articles.summary: Arsenal came from behind to beat Chelsea 2-1 at the Emirates after a fantastic, fiercely contested London derby between two well-matched sides.The Gunners re...
articles.body:
Arsenal came from behind to beat Chelsea 2-1 at the Emirates after a fantastic, fiercely contested London derby between two well-matched sides.

The Gunners recovered from a nightmare opening minute before goals from Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard turned the game around, while David Raya produced several huge saves to protect Arsenal's lead late on.

Arsenal could hardly have made a worse start, with Morgan Rogers putting Chelsea ahead inside the opening minute.

The response was strong. Bukayo Saka was soon causing problems down the right and won a dangerous free kick before Arsenal thought they had equalised through Riccardo Calafiori in the 11th minute, only for the goal to be ruled out for offside.

Kai Havertz then had a header comfortably saved, while Saka also tested Martinez as Arsenal continued to push. Chelsea remained dangerous at the other end, however, with Raya called into action against Cole Palmer and Reece James.

Arsenal finally got their reward in the 25th minute when Havertz found the net to make it 1-1.

The game remained wonderfully open, with both teams looking capable of scoring. Myles Lewis-Skelly had an effort deflected wide, while tempers also began to rise as the London derby edge became increasingly apparent.

Chelsea almost regained the lead just before the interval when Neto struck the post, but Arsenal survived to go in level at 1-1.

(Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Odegaard strikes before Raya takes centre stage

Arsenal flew out of the blocks after the restart and needed only four minutes to complete the turnaround.

Martin Odegaard scored in the 49th minute to put the Gunners 2-1 ahead, immediately changing the complexion of the game.

Saka had opportunities to extend the advantage, shooting straight at Martinez in the 55th minute before forcing another save later in the half.

Chelsea were certainly not finished, though, and Raya became increasingly important. The Arsenal goalkeeper made two crucial saves in quick succession around the hour mark, including one to deny Palmer.

Mikel Arteta freshened things up in the 66th minute, with Piero Hincapie replacing Calafiori and Martin Zubimendi coming on for Lewis-Skelly.

Arsenal continued to threaten, but the final stages became increasingly tense. Viktor Gyokeres replaced Havertz and Mikel Merino came on for Odegaard in the 76th minute, as the Gunners attempted to see out the victory.

Raya was required again from a Chelsea corner in the 79th minute before producing arguably his biggest stop of the match in the 88th minute, making an exceptional save to deny Estevao.

Noni Madueke replaced Saka shortly afterwards and, following four minutes of added time, Arsenal had done enough.

A superb London derby, with the score as we predicted earlier today ! A big comeback and another three points for the Gunners. Chelsea pushed Arsenal all the way, but Odegaard's second-half goal and some outstanding goalkeeping from Raya proved decisive.

articles.title: Games like Louisville vs Ole Miss could become a Labor Day tradition in Nashville | Estes
articles.summary: Promotions for the Louisville-Ole Miss game at Nissan Stadium called the Music City Kickoff 'a new tradition' for Nashville. Will that be the case?
articles.body:
A quick glance around Week 1's college football schedule was all it took to notice how high-stakes, highly anticipated opening games between big-name, out-of-conference opponents are nearing extinction.

Most opening matchups stunk in 2026 for major-conference teams, ending up as blowouts.

Labor Day weekend offered only one game in which both teams were ranked in the Associated Press' preseason media poll. That game happened to be in Nashville, with Ole Miss and Louisville each traveling a little ways for a nationally televised, Sunday night contest at Nissan Stadium.

It certainly wasn't the venue that lured them here. Old Nissan Stadium, to borrow a line from colleague Terry McCormick, feels like a car about to be traded in, needing a lot of repair work that'll never happen. This game, too, wasn't just two schools sitting down and settling on a common location on a map.

Nah, this is bigger plans in motion. This game has a title sponsor. And maybe a future. And definitely an emu.

The Liberty Mutual Music City Kickoff , they are calling it, and it's not intended to be a one-time occasion.

As the Nashville Sports Council's web page promoting this game has teased, "A new tradition begins in Music City." Sounds like there could be high-quality, season-opening college football games like these for years to come in a new Nissan Stadium.

"That would be the goal," said Scott Ramsey, Sports Council CEO and President. "In working with the (Tennessee) Titans , kind of in lockstep on this one, I really hope we can."

No guarantees, Ramsey cautioned. Not in this era of rampant uncertainty in college sports.

But the city, clearly, is viewing Labor Day weekend as a college sports opportunity on multiple fronts. The Louisville-Ole Miss football game was only part of a sports weekend including a nationally televised volleyball doubleheader at Bridgestone Arena. The "Broadway Block Party" was set to feature Louisville-Texas followed by Tennessee-Indiana.

Ideas are in the works to try to bring the NCAA women's soccer championships to Geodis Park or perhaps the NCAA women's volleyball championship to Bridgestone Arena. That's per Ramsey, who also said that Nashville will bid to extend the two-year agreement for the FCS national title football game at Vanderbilt's FirstBank Stadium.

"We feel like Labor Day is an opportunity, a little bit like FCS was in January, to take a weekend that the city could host an event and a game, and we could kind of turn it into a multi-day activity," Ramsey said.

That makes sense. With FBS bowl games increasingly under threat (and even more so if the playoff expands to 24 teams), establishing an annual, big-time Labor Day football weekend is an alluring and proactive move for a mid-tier bowl city like Nashville.

A good template would be the annual Aflac kickoff game – or games – held in Atlanta.

You know, those games where winning coaches and players end up wearing that silly leather helmet?

The Atlanta kickoff games date back nearly two decades . Beginning with Nick Saban's burgeoning powerhouse at Alabama opening back-to-back seasons at the old Georgia Dome, beating Clemson in 2008 and Virginia Tech in 2009, this event has welcomed 22 different SEC teams and 20 ACC teams.

It's no coincidence that the Atlanta game has trafficked heavily in SEC and ACC teams. It's geography, for one, but it's also because those conferences have TV deals with ESPN/ABC. (Unlike, say, the Big Ten and FOX).

Louisville and Ole Miss, too, opened the season against each other in Atlanta in 2021.

Five years later, here they are in Nashville. And they won't be the last ones, reportedly.

Georgia and Florida State have agreed to play in Nashville in 2028 (per a June report from Warchant.com ), but there's still room in the new stadium for 2027.

"We're working on something for next year," Ramsey said. "Then once you get to '29 and beyond, because it's a regular-season game, you've got to deal with two ADs, two head coaches, two conference offices and two (television) rights-holders, to some degree."

One could look at this Louisville-Ole Miss game and at the massive domed stadium nearly complete next door and see a strong future for season-opening showcases like these in Nashville.

"Scheduling a regular-season game in the future, multiple years out, is really difficult to 100% say for sure, 'Yes, we're going to do it every year,' " Ramsey said, "just because you just don't know how the scheduling is going to change within these conferences. …

"Right now, (a few years) seems to be 100 years out."

articles.title: No. 13 Maryland field hockey shocks No. 6 Duke in 3-2 shootout victory
articles.summary: The Terps sweep the weekend and remain perfect to start the season.
articles.body:
The battle between No. 13 Maryland field hockey and No. 6 Duke was everything fans could've asked for, as the former ACC foes went toe-to-toe on a neutral site for 70 minutes and into a shootout.

Thanks to a late goal from freshman Ella Beach and three consecutive shootout saves from goalkeeper Alyssa Klebasko, the Terps stunned the Blue Devils, 3-2, to move to 4-0 on the season.

Duke had the first major chance just three minutes into the match, as Shae Wozniak received a centering pass just on the doorsteps of the goal. The attempt was denied by Klebasko, who dropped into a split and made a kick save with her left blocker.

Once again, penalty corners were a major theme throughout the game. Maryland had a pair of them right off the bat, but Duke set the tone by blocking a pair of hits from Feliz Kuhne.

On the other side, Duke earned a pair of penalty corners two minutes later and broke through on the second attempt. While the Blue Devils botched the initial insert, they quickly recovered and sent another centering pass towards the middle where Ashley Stockdale tipped the ball past Klebasko to put the Blue Devils ahead.

Later in the frame, Juliette Schulten received a penalty corner insert and ripped a bullet shot past Klebasko to double Duke's lead with 90 seconds to play in the quarter.

Duke doubled up Maryland in the penalty corner category, 10-5, but had little success after the opening period, failing to capitalize the rest of the way.

Despite the early hole, Maryland bounced back quickly with a familiar sight: Francisca Eschoyez scoring off a penalty corner. The Quinnipiac transfer notched her fourth goal off a set piece to halve Duke's lead not even two minutes into the second quarter.

Following Maryland's goal, the defenses settled in. Each team had a few chances throughout the period but couldn't break through, sending the game to halftime with Duke ahead, 2-1.

Coming out of halftime, Duke had a trio of opportunities to re-extend its lead, but Maryland's defense stood tall again. Klebasko made another fantastic kick save on a shot from Kyle Massey in the 36th minute, then registered another denial when she knocked down a ball that popped up in the air. On Duke's third attempt, Erin Callahan blocked a shot from the top of the circle.

While Klebasko conceded a pair of early goals, she responded well as the game rolled on. She finished with three saves in regulation and added three more in the shootout to clinch the victory.

While neither team scored in the third quarter, it was a stretch undeniably controlled by Duke. The Blue Devils dominated the time of possession and made it difficult for the Terps to generate any offense.

Early in the fourth, Duke was called for a yellow card, but with the door open, Maryland failed to register a shot for the entire five-minute penalty. In fact, the Terps didn't have a look on net until the 58th minute, when Rachael Whitehead launched the ball towards the cage from 25 yards away. Fortunately for the Terps, that's all they needed, as Beach redirected Whitehead's long-range missile into the back of the net to send the match to overtime.

The remarkable goal – Beach's first of her collegiate career – came with the Terps down a player under a yellow card.

In the overtime period, Duke had the majority of the possession but couldn't find the winner, as a pair of shots sailed over the crossbar.

1. Dealing with adversity. Maryland trailed for the first time all season – by two goals no less – in Sunday's game, but fought back against a top-10 opponent. Today's victory could be one the Terps and their fans look back on later in the year as a season-defining moment.

2. Exorcising the demons. The Terps defeated the Blue Devils for the first time since 2022. Maryland still holds the overall series advantage, 37-17-3.

3. Top-10 takedown. Maryland gets its first win against a top-10 opponent in its first chance to do so this season. In 2025, the Terps went just 1-5 against top-10 opponents, a record that contributed to their vacancy from the NCAA tournament.

articles.title: Colorado Rockies vs. St Louis Cardinals game discussion: Kyle Leahy vs. Tanner Gordon
articles.summary: The Rockies will look to take the rubber match and tie the season series.
articles.body:
After a couple of crazy games — one loss and one win — the Rockies will look to take their final game against the St. Louis Cardinals in this afternoon's rubber match. If they win, they will tie the season series 3-3.

The Rockies have played 19 rubber matches so far this season and are 6-13, the second-worst rubber match winning percentage (.316) behind the Boston Red Sox (5-14, .263). Seven of their rubber match losses have come by two or fewer runs, and they are 3-5 in home rubber matches (3-8 on the road). Wednesday's rubber match against the Orioles marked the first time the Rockies have won three-straight rubber matches since winning five-straight May 7-June 25, 2023.

Tanner Gordon (1-4, 5.18 ERA) will take the mound for the Rockies. Gordon was on a roll in his last outing before being stymied by a one-hour and 38-minute rain delay. Gordon managed to toss five innings before the delay, only allowing three hits and one run with one walk and three strikeouts. But he only threw 60 pitches, so hopefully that means he'll be fresh this afternoon. He has faced the Cardinals twice (one start) and is 1-1 with a 1.93 ERA in 9.1 innings.

Gordon will face Colorado Mesa product, and Boulder native, Kyle Leahy (10-4, 3.13 ERA). Leahy is in his fourth MLB season, but first where all of his appearances have been starts. He made 98 appearances from 2023-2025, but only one start — the Cardinals' final game against the Chicago Cubs last September where he pitched three perfect innings with a strikeout. In his last outing against the Pittsburgh Pirates, Leahy pitched three innings and allowed one run (a solo homer) on four hits with one walk and three strikeouts. He has faced the Rockies six times in his career, and started against them this year on August 7th in St. Louis. He is 2-0 against them with a 4.05 ERA in 13.1 innings.

articles.summary: Richard Hughes has left Liverpool as sporting director. Now an awful plan can follow him out of the door.It's the end of the Richard Hughes era at Anfield. H...
articles.body:
Richard Hughes has left Liverpool as sporting director. Now an awful plan can follow him out of the door.

It's the end of the Richard Hughes era at Anfield. He's no longer the Liverpool sporting director and the Reds will move forward with new ideas running the show.

The Hughes era will go down as a strange one. One of the strangest, in fact, as Liverpool tore up a title-winning team and replaced it in controversial fashion. The remaining squad looks unbalanced and has three nine-figure signings in it - a strange combination to say the least.

But the gameplan under Hughes has been strange. Liverpool moved away from their model that saw them sign players for the positions they needed them - or rather, where Jürgen Klopp needed them.

Instead, the 'manager' role became the 'head coach' role. The club signed the 'best' players available and then asked a coach to make the best possible team out of them, something Arne Slot found impossible last season.

And looking at this current squad, it's difficult to believe that this is the best possible squad for Iraola to get a tune out of. Is having four natural left-wingers better than having a fit right-back and a natural defensive midfielder?

That was never the case under Klopp. Go back to his last summer in 2023 and a desperate search for a defensive midfielder saw Liverpool land a surprise signing in Wataru Endo. Not a player who would have been anywhere near the shortlist this summer.

But Endo was brilliant in that campaign and brought exactly what the manager needed.

Overall, though, there are conflicting ideas at play. Liverpool hired Iraola because they wanted someone with his style of play, with a system that works, and felt he was what the team needed.

Then, however, they sign players without a set system in mind and ask him to adapt. Why hire a manager with a certain style of play if what you actually want is incredible levels of pragmatism? People have spent all summer talking about 'Iraola' style players but the club don't appear to have cared whatsoever about that idea.

"I think we've preferred at the end to have the best players, probably, than a player that maybe is specifically for that [right-sided] position," he said, per the Guardian .

That's a plan that doesn't make sense at the top level. The most successful clubs in recent years have been Liverpool, Manchester City and Arsenal. Three clubs who all saw the benefit of having managers in place with a strong say in transfer direction.

In fact, no other club has mounted a serious title challenge in nearly a decade. The only way the idea makes sense is with a series of pragmatic coaches who will happily adapt their way of doing things to suit whoever the club sings, i.e. Carlo Ancelotti.

But Liverpool don't want that kind of coach, either. They want someone with a style of play they can rally behind - but not sign players specifically for.

Putting faith in the manager or head coach, letting them have the players they need to make things work, and that being how the sporting director shines - finding those players - is a model that currently dominates the Premier League. Liverpool moved away from it under Hughes and now is their chance to fix that.

articles.body:
The first full weekend of college football wraps up Sunday with two marquee matchups featuring four teams making their season debuts.

Louisville and Ole Miss will meet in Nashville in the day's only matchup between ranked teams, while Notre Dame and Wisconsin take the field at Lambeau Field later in the evening.

For today's TST Best Bets, we are targeting the spread in both games as we look to finish the first full weekend of college football on a high note.

First Pick: Ole Miss -6.5 over Louisville

Rundown: This line is asking Ole Miss to win by a touchdown in Nashville, and we are comfortable laying the points with the team that has significantly more continuity under center.

Trinidad Chambliss returns after throwing for 3,937 yards with 22 touchdowns and just three interceptions last season, leading Ole Miss on a run to the College Football Playoff semifinals. He will also have Kewan Lacy beside him after the running back piled up 1,567 yards and a school-record 24 rushing touchdowns.

Louisville can lean on Isaac Brown, who averaged 8.8 yards per carry in an injury-shortened 2025 season, but its passing game is far less proven. Ohio State transfer Lincoln Kienholz enters his first season as a full-time starter with only 250 career passing yards and one touchdown.

The Cardinals have enough talent to make this competitive, but Chambliss gives Ole Miss a major advantage in a season opener filled with unknowns. Expect the Rebels to pull away as the game progresses and cover the 6.5 points.

Second Pick: Notre Dame -21 over Wisconsin

Rundown: Wisconsin's defense may keep this respectable early, but its offense has a long way to go after averaging just 12.8 points per game last season. The Badgers scored 10 or fewer seven times, leaving almost no room for error against one of the country's best teams.

Old Dominion transfer Colton Joseph gives Wisconsin some much-needed playmaking ability, but he is stepping up in competition and debuting in a new offense. Notre Dame has far fewer questions at quarterback with CJ Carr returning after throwing for 2,741 yards and 24 touchdowns in his first season as the starter.

The Irish won eight games by more than 20 points last year, while half of Wisconsin's losses came by at least three touchdowns. Even without Jeremiyah Love and Jadarian Price, Notre Dame should score enough to turn another quiet game from the Badgers into a comfortable cover.
